1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.
LAC no. 402/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Rishi Pal Vs. Union of India Page no. 2 of 12 2.

sentences.text:
The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 bighas 01 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 6//13 (108), 18 (414), 23 (416), 8//4 (108), 7 (416), 8 (416), 10//7/2 (304), i.e.
total area measuring 25 Bigha LAC no. 402/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))

Rishi Pal Vs.
Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 and 02 Biswas, having share as per the revenue record, situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi (in short, the said land).

sentences.text:
It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to reassess the market value of the land which has been wrongly assessed by the LAC.
6. Following are the grounds under which the reference petition has been filed :
i) The land of the petitioner is situated in Village Mubarakpur Dabas and is well connected with metaled roads from all sides and at the time of acquisition was having great potential value as residential and commercial.

The land of petitioner is levelled and as such gives handsome crops income 2-3 times in a year to the petitioner and some part of the land is developed as colony and the petitioners also claims for loss of livelihood and also loss of income interalia on the following amongst other grounds.
ii) The land of the petitioner is situated near the National Highway No. 10, Rohtak Road, Delhi and has great potential value as a perfect Building/ Commercial site.
Commercial and Residential activities have commenced all around the land of the petitioner and are going on since more than 12 years.

All kinds of civic amenities like electricity, water, road, bus service, telephone, school, college, LAC no. 402/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Rishi Pal Vs. Union of India Page no. 4 of 12 etc are easily available to the land of the petitioners,

entities.text: Rishi Pal Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the land of petitioners has great value being developed and a perfect residential and commercial site.
iii) The Land of the petitioners is approachable by metaled road and is very close to Nangloi township and Mundka Industrial Area and the same were fully developed at the time of notification.

There are many residential colonies such as Bhagya Vihar, Mir Vihar, Jain Colony and Rama Vihar,
etc which are existing since 1993 near the land of the petitioner and Govt. is also going to regularise the said buildings and provide all the civic amenities thereafter.
Therefore, the price of the acquired land should have been assessed minimum @ Rs 10,000/- per sq. yards.

iv) The land of the petitioners have been covered by the other revenue estate such as Rani Khera,
Madan Pur Dabas, Karala and Mazri which are well developed by way of construction of colonies and have great potential value.
Moreover, the petitioners have solid proof regarding the higher market value of land which is not less than Rs. 10,000/- and the same may be produced at the time of evidence before the Court.

It is also alleged that the Government police has not been properly implemented because the indicative price fixed by the Government is totally wrong and illegal and the same should be ratify and compensation be paid to the petitioners.
v) The Government Policy has not been properly implemented because the indicative price fixed by the Government is totally wrong LAC no. 402/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))
Rishi Pal Vs. Union of India Page no. 5 of 12 and illegal.

It is further prayed that the reference as to the inadequacy of compensation may kindly be referred to Ld. District Judge for adjudication.
Petitioners also prayed for the recovery of the cost of the petition alongwith any other order deemed fit and proper be also passed in favor of the petitioner.

8. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 /UOI and, it is, inter alia,
submitted that the notification under Section 4 was passed on 21.03.2003 and the declaration under Section 6 of the Act was issued on 19.03.2004 and the said land has been acquired for the public purposes i.e. for Planned Development of Delhi.

It is submitted that the learned LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view all the aspects and has assessed the market value after considering the level of development, locality and situation of the area where the said land is situated.

The Ld. LAC has assessed the fair market value of the said land by adopting the indicative price fixed by the government of NCT of LAC no. 402/ 2016 (Award No. 16/2005 06/DC(NW)) Rishi Pal Vs. sentences.text: It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.

12. It is stated that the possession of the said land has been taken over by the DDA on 04.04.2006 and after taking possession, the same was LAC no. 402/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))

19. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

sentences.text:
In the case of Savitri Devi (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 as Rs. 19,45,800/
per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Savitri Devi (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
21. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 22.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2)
Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
LAC no. 402/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Rishi Pal Vs. Union of India Page no. 11 of 12 (3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
